open_points.subject: M30 FormFieldRefusalKind table
open_points.text: The release: the form refusal table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What imported constant will expose the form-refusal correspondence to generated consumers?
options: Choose another explicitly declared imported constant for the table.
consequences: Keeping FORM_FIELD_REFUSAL_KINDS preserves the previously explicit import path.
A different name is valid only if generation declares it and all consumers use it; without a named constant, generated code must guess the table's symbol or duplicate its policy.
open_points.requirement: A row of the form refusal table: the kind of refusal a value outside its form is answered with, by the form field it was given as — a field of a closed list answers `outside_closed_list`, every other field `outside_form`.

open_points.subject: M31 ProjectStatusConfirmation table
open_points.text: The release: the project confirmation table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What imported constant will expose the project-status-to-confirmed-action correspondence to generated consumers?
options: Choose another explicitly declared imported constant for the table.
consequences: Keeping PROJECT_STATUS_CONFIRMATIONS preserves the previously explicit import path.
A different name requires generation and every consumer to agree on it; leaving the symbol unnamed forces the generator to invent the import or encode the correspondence independently.
open_points.requirement: A row of the project confirmation table: the confirmed action a project's card offers by the project's status — archiving an active project (V1-7, R0-12), erasing an archived one (R0-60).

open_points.subject: M32 ImportFormFailureField table
open_points.text: The release: the import form failure table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What imported constant will expose the form-field-to-mapping-field correspondence to generated consumers?
options: Choose another explicitly declared imported constant for the table.
consequences: Keeping IMPORT_FORM_FIELD_MAPPING_FIELDS preserves the previously explicit import path.
A different name must be declared and used consistently; without one, the generator must guess where the correspondence lives or reproduce it locally.
open_points.requirement: A row of the import form failure table: the field of the import mapping a value's form failure is reported under, by the form field the value was checked as (R0-85) — an alias under the alias, a customer kind under the customer kind.

open_points.subject: M33 CustomerEligibilityRefusal table
open_points.text: The release: the customer eligibility refusal table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What imported constant will expose the eligibility-to-refusal correspondence to generated consumers?
options: Choose another explicitly declared imported constant for the table.
consequences: Keeping CUSTOMER_ELIGIBILITY_REFUSALS preserves the previously explicit import path.
A different name works only when generation declares it and consumers import it; an unnamed table forces generated code to guess or duplicate the refusal policy.
open_points.requirement: A row of the customer eligibility refusal table: the kind of refusal a project's customer is refused with, by the customer's eligibility — an erased, restricted or ended customer (R0-16, R0-51, R0-57).

open_points.subject: M34 StoreCompanionStepSuffix table
open_points.text: The release: the store companion table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What imported constant will expose the discard-step-to-file-suffix correspondence to generated consumers?
options: Choose another explicitly declared imported constant for the table.
consequences: Keeping STORE_COMPANION_STEP_SUFFIXES preserves the previously explicit import path.
A different name must be declared and imported consistently; without a symbol, the generator must invent the suffix table's location or hard-code its values.
open_points.requirement: A row of the store companion table: the suffix of the companion file a step of discarding a new store removes, by that step — the write-ahead log, the shared memory and the journal.

set_aside.subject: M29 OwnerFormField table
set_aside.text: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
set_aside.question: What imported constant will expose this table to generated consumers?
options: Export it under another explicitly declared constant name and make every consumer import that name.
consequences: OWNER_FORM_FIELDS restores a concrete path from the release table to generated code.
Another name works only if generation and every consuming note use the same declared symbol; otherwise the generator must invent an import or the table remains unreachable.
set_aside.requirement: A row of the owner form table: one field of the owner's pages — what the owner types or picks in a form — as the owner interface names it on the page and reads it back (owner, 2026-11-25): its name, whether it belongs to the owner's request itself or to the values the owner gives, and how its text is read: as text, as a whole number, as yes or no, or as one of a closed list.
